title: One product photo went into Codex and a complete Amazon launch came out
description:
Someone gave an AI one product photo and one prompt, and got back a complete Amazon launch. Listing images, UGC ads, commercials, thumbnails, everything.

The stack is OpenAI's Codex, their open-source coding agent, plus Higgsfield's official skills pack. Install the skills and Codex suddenly knows content formats: UGC ads, cinematic commercials, CGI product demos. It plans the shots, calls over 30 image and video models like Seedance 2.0, Veo 3.1 and Kling 3.0, and runs the whole project like an employee you supervise. And yes, I'm the Claude guy, which is exactly why you should hear this: the setup is genuinely good. The same skills pack also works inside Claude Code and Cursor, it auto-detects whichever agent you run.

The honest part: renders bill against your Higgsfield plan, and the first pass needs your taste. You're the creative director, the AI is the crew. The creator behind this says his bill runs about a tenth of what Claude Code costs him. His numbers, not mine.

Comment CODEX and I'll send you both links, the agent and the skills pack. Follow for more AI that actually matters.
